---
title: Checkpoints, EMA, and resuming
description: "Save and load artifacts, average parameters with EMA, and resume a run from a full checkpoint."
---

Save a model artifact for inference, serving, representation export, or
adaptation in another fit. Keep a full Lightning checkpoint to resume the
training run. Optional EMA maintains an averaged copy of the parameters. This
page covers all three, continuing with `model` from
[Train and save](../learn/train-and-save.qmd).
[Training options](training-options.qmd) covers the fit call itself.

## Save and load

Use a RelFlow artifact to retain the schema and learned model state:

```python
import relflow as rf

model.save("artifacts/payment-history.rf")
loaded = rf.Model.load("artifacts/payment-history.rf")
prediction_data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    predict="payments/history/requests.parquet",
)
predictions = loaded.predict(datamodule=prediction_data, batch_size=256, devices=1)
```

The application supplies `payments/history/requests.parquet` as a Parquet file.
Prediction records omit `disputed` from every transaction.

The artifact contains the state dictionary, schema, batch size, and producing
RelFlow version. State includes field-owned buffers such as vocabularies and
normalizers. `load` constructs the model on CPU. Move it to the intended device
for direct inference; Lightning owns placement when using its loops.

A `Model.save` artifact does not contain optimizer or scheduler state, Trainer
progress, data sources, or processor configuration. Supply those explicitly
when fitting a loaded model. Compilation is transient and must be requested
again after loading.

The artifact carries the model's generated architecture and learned state.
The [serving runtime](serving.qmd) loads that model into an HTTP application;
hosts, process supervision, and ingress configuration belong to the
infrastructure running that application.

### Checkpoint compatibility

Saved weights must match the model architecture used to load them. Loading
incompatible weights raises an error; there is no automatic conversion.

## Average learned parameters with EMA

Payment-review validation scores can vary as optimization moves the learned
parameters. Exponential moving averaging (EMA) evaluates a smoothed parameter
history. It is optional; compare it with ordinary training on the same
held-out payments before adopting it. For this fit, `datamodule` supplies the
training and validation splits as in [Training options](training-options.qmd#fit-a-model).

```python
model.fit(
    datamodule,
    batch_size=128,
    learning_rate=1e-4,
    max_epochs=30,
    callbacks=[rf.EMA(decay=0.99)],
    checkpoint_dir="checkpoints/payments-ema",
)
```

`rf.EMA` defaults to `decay=0.99`. Decay must be finite and satisfy
`0 <= decay < 1`. A larger decay gives older updates more influence after
warmup. Averaging follows optimizer updates, so accumulating more batches
before an update does not itself advance EMA.

EMA smooths learned parameters, while vocabulary and normalization state keep
their current values. Averaging restarts for parameters replaced by model or
vocabulary changes. It consumes additional model memory, including during
validation; include it when checking whether a training configuration fits.

During fitting, validation uses averaged parameters and restores live
parameters afterward so optimization can continue. Early stopping and rollback
therefore select using the averaged model's validation score. Fitting ends
with averaged parameters; default rollback restores the best selected averaged
checkpoint. With `rollback=False`, the returned model retains the final
average. Use that returned model or its saved artifact for subsequent test and
prediction. Adding EMA only to standalone evaluation does not create an
average of a past training run.

### Save and resume EMA training

`rf.Model.load(...)` reads an EMA checkpoint's averaged model for inference.
Full Lightning checkpoints also preserve the information needed to continue
training. Resume with a fresh EMA callback and the full checkpoint:

```python
checkpoint = "checkpoints/payments-ema/last.ckpt"
resumed = rf.Model.load(checkpoint)
resume_data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    train="payments/history/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/history/validation.parquet",
)
resumed.fit(
    resume_data,
    batch_size=128,
    learning_rate=1e-4,
    max_epochs=60,
    callbacks=[rf.EMA(decay=0.99)],
    ckpt_path=checkpoint,
)
```

Use the actual checkpoint path produced by the run. Recreate the optimizer
and any scheduler configuration as in [Resume Training](#resume-training).
Loading the model alone and calling `fit` without `ckpt_path` starts a new
run from its exported averaged parameters. Resuming restores the saved decay.
EMA rejects checkpoint callbacks configured with
`save_weights_only=True`; use full checkpoints, including for recovery saves.
A `model.save(...)` artifact stores the current inference model but cannot
resume the EMA or optimizer history.

## Resume training

The default rollback callback saves best and last full checkpoints at its
validation/epoch checkpoints. The best model is selected for its validation
score; the last checkpoint preserves the most recent state saved by that
callback. For recovery between validation checks, attach a separate unmonitored
checkpoint callback:

```python
from lightning.pytorch.callbacks import ModelCheckpoint

recovery = ModelCheckpoint(
    dirpath="checkpoints/recovery",
    filename="step-{step}",
    monitor=None,
    every_n_train_steps=1_000,
    save_top_k=1,
    save_last=True,
)
model.fit(datamodule, callbacks=[recovery])
```

The recovery checkpoint contains optimizer and scheduler state. Its step
schedule does not select the best model using a previous validation score;
the built-in rollback callback continues to select from fresh validation checks.

Use a full Lightning checkpoint to resume optimizer/scheduler state and loop
progress. Recreate the runtime configuration and pass the checkpoint to `fit`:

```python
resumed = rf.Model.load("checkpoints/recovery/last.ckpt")
resume_data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    train="payments/history/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/history/validation.parquet",
)
resumed.fit(
    resume_data,
    batch_size=128,
    learning_rate=1e-3,
    max_epochs=100,
    ckpt_path="checkpoints/recovery/last.ckpt",
)
```

Recreate any scheduler and keep optimizer configuration consistent with the
saved run. `rf.Model.load` restores model state; the `ckpt_path` argument is
what tells Lightning to resume training state.

Another `fit` call without `ckpt_path` starts a new optimizer run from the current
model state. Use the best full checkpoint to continue with optimizer and
scheduler state matching the restored best model. A new ordinary fit after
rollback creates AdamW on the restored parameters automatically. Supply any
scheduler again for that new run.

The saved artifact is what [Serving](serving.qmd) loads, and what
[Reusable representations](../learn/reusable-representations.qmd) reopens to
export context. If a run fails, [Troubleshooting](../reference/troubleshooting.qmd)
lists the first checks for checkpoint and EMA errors.
